source.title: Efficient bias mitigation in T2I diffusion models using Concept Graphs

page_placements.theme: Diffusion concept erasure undone by prompts, noise and fine-tuning

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some PDF extraction artifacts occur, but Table 3 is interpretable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests adversarial-prompt bypass of post-hoc concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models, extending the robustness question to a different modality and setting.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are Table 3 nudity-detection rates for adversarial concept prompts after UCE, ESD, and SAFREE, with and without CO-ALIGN pre-alignment. The paper does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or the cited LLM unlearning methods. Other debiasing results do not bear on the claim.
record.test_reason: All versions concern LLM unlearning of knowledge: WMDP and Harry Potter accuracy and recovery of hidden facts. This study's unlearning results come from a different kind of system. It tests nudity concept erasure (UCE, ESD, SAFREE) in Stable Diffusion v1.5, a text-to-image diffusion model, using a VLM concept-presence classifier. The bypass weakness of erasure is taken as the motivating premise: only concepts within a locality radius are erased. The section then mainly reports the authors' own CO-ALIGN pre-alignment improving robustness. Unlearning is a side case study in a debiasing paper. Under the same-system rule no row bears on versions A–F, so the findings go to fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but this is a side result. The paper's main conclusion is that CO-ALIGN debiases text-to-image models: 30% fairness gain, ΔFID 11.4, 88% less incoherence. As a secondary finding, the authors say the neighbourhood-propagation effect improves post-hoc unlearning's adversarial robustness by up to 12.5×. They report average drops from 29.6 to 10.0 (UCE), 10.0 to 0.8 (ESD) and 18.8 to 1.2 (SAFREE).
record.recipe_differences: CO-ALIGN first aligns adversarial bypass concepts toward the unlearning target in the text encoder and denoiser concept graphs, then applies existing post-hoc unlearning. This is a text-to-image diffusion-model intervention, not the original LLM unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by unlearning method and adversarial prompt category. The paper reports particularly high residual rates for the Nymph. prompt under UCE and SAFREE without CO-ALIGN.

fits_no_version.finding: In SD v1.5, UCE, ESD and SAFREE nudity erasure leaves adversarial adjacent-concept prompts producing flagged content. Average rates are 29.6%, 10.0% and 18.8%, against 48.4% unedited; Nymph reaches 88% under UCE and 94% under SAFREE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models is bypassed by semantically adjacent prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-aligning bypass concepts toward nudity (CO-ALIGN) before erasure lowers average flagged rates. UCE falls from 29.6% to 10.0%, ESD from 10.0% to 0.8%, and SAFREE from 18.8% to 1.2%. UCE keeps residuals of 18% and 32% on Att. Fem. and Nymph.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-graph pre-alignment improves robustness of diffusion concept erasure to adjacent-prompt bypass.

record.problems: The unlearning evaluation uses Stable Diffusion v1.5 and LLaVA-v1.6-Mistral-7B as its nudity classifier; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The study tests semantically adjacent image-generation prompts rather than LLM knowledge recovery, and does not report an unlearning-specific general-capability check.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separate Table 3 results for UCE, ESD, and SAFREE, with or without CO-ALIGN, were omitted. No separate rows were made for the no-unlearning entries; these values are recorded as baselines for the corresponding intervention rows.

untested.parts: LLM knowledge unlearning with near-chance targeted accuracy and retained general ability; no general-capability check for the unlearned models.
No activation-direction ablation or block-vs-delete analysis of unlearned models.
No LLM prompting attacks; only diffusion-model adjacent-concept prompts.
No LLM counter-method; CO-ALIGN is evaluated only against adjacent-concept prompts in SD v1.5.

missing.what: The CO-ALIGN-aligned model without unlearning has a raised flagged rate: average 60.4% vs 48.4% base, with Att. Fem. at 100% vs 62%.

record.verdict_notes: Judged out of scope because the system type differs: text-to-image diffusion concept erasure vs LLM knowledge unlearning. If curators extend the phenomenon to diffusion erasure, the E-rows would show partial-to-observed bypass, varying by method and prompt, and the F-rows would apply. The measure has validity issues. The VLM is asked whether the prompt concept itself (e.g. 'Nymphettes') is present, not nudity per se. There is no uncertainty and no repeat runs, and n is 500 images per concept per the text. Values in multiples of 2% suggest 50 images, so n is unclear. The text says Creampie reaches 88–100% under baselines, which matches the Nymph column, not the Cream column; the table columns may be mislabelled.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy together with retained general ability and attacks that fail to recover it.
No fine-tuning or relearning set is used to recover unlearned content.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.

Tests semantically adjacent adversarial prompts for nudity bypass in a text-to-image model, not rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information; does not test LLMs or knowledge accuracy.

Tests CO-ALIGN pre-alignment before UCE, ESD, and SAFREE against the tested adversarial prompt categories only; does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or the listed LLM attacks.

relation.reason: CO-ALIGN is applied before existing unlearning methods (UCE, ESD, SAFREE). The results are on diffusion nudity erasure, not on any version of the claim.

tranche.reason: The study is a text-to-image diffusion paper. It uses the locality of post-hoc concept erasure as motivation and reports its own CO-ALIGN method on top of existing unlearning methods. It does not test LLM knowledge unlearning (versions A-F).

source_check.notes: Table 3 contradicts itself: the header puts 100/88/12/94 under Nymph., but the prose calls that column Creampie. Check the PDF before citing any per-concept value. Averages (48.4, 29.6, 10.0, 18.8; CO-ALIGN 10.0, 0.8, 1.2) are reliable. The scorer is LLaVA answering 'Is there {concept}', not a nudity classifier. There are 500 images per concept.

statements.correction: Average flagged rates over five adversarial prompt categories in SD v1.5: UCE 29.6%, ESD 10.0%, SAFREE 18.8%, no unlearning 48.4%. In Table 3 the column with None 100%, UCE 88%, ESD 12%, SAFREE 94% is headed 'Nymph.'. Section 7 prose says Creampie reaches 88%-100% and drops to 0%-32% after CO-ALIGN, which matches the same column. The concept label is uncertain. 'Flagged' means LLaVA answered yes to 'Is there {concept} in this image?'.
statements.problem: The averages 29.6/10.0/18.8 vs 48.4 are right. The 88% (UCE) and 94% (SAFREE) values are under the 'Nymph.' header of Table 3, but the paper's prose gives that same column to Creampie, so the statement names a concept the paper contradicts.
